note: Machine half of references/compliance.md (same ids). Regexes are case-insensitive and run on NFKC-normalized text.

rules.title: Payment amount is a Reg Z trigger term
rules.message: Stating a payment amount requires the down payment, the repayment terms and the APR in the same post. Usual fix: drop the payment amount. Otherwise add your compliance-approved APR example (apr_disclosure).

rules.title: Down payment amount or percent (house policy: treated like a trigger term)
rules.message: Official commentary limits the down payment trigger to credit sales and says 'no down payment' is not a trigger (Reg Z comment 24(d)(1)-1). Many lenders still treat '3% down' as a trigger in mortgage ads. Flagged so you decide with your compliance team: drop the number ('low down payment options') or add your approved APR example. 'Zero down' and 'no money down' are not flagged.
rules.source: Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.24(d)(1)(i) and Official Interpretation comment 24(d)(1)-1

rules.title: Number of payments or loan term offered with credit
if_any: \b(get|offer|offering|lock|qualify for|available|apply for|we have|you can get|ask (me|us) about)\b[^.\n]{0,40}\b\d{2}[- ]year (loan|mortgage|fixed|term)
rules.message: A number of payments or a term ('30-year mortgage', '360 payments', 'pay it off in 15 years') is a trigger term (Reg Z comment 24(d)(1)-2 lists '30-year mortgage'). Reporting a survey average ('the average 30-year fixed rate in Freddie Mac's survey') is treated by this bundle as market news; that is the bundle's interpretation, confirm it with your compliance team.

rules.title: A rate offered by you must be stated as an APR
if_any: \b(as low as|starting at|rates? from|our rates?|my rates?|we can (get|offer)|lock (in )?(at|your rate at)?|get you)\b[^.\n]{0,30}\d+(\.\d+)?\s?%
rules.message: If the post states a rate you offer, it must state it as an annual percentage rate (APR), with the other terms the trigger rules require. Without an approved example, do not state your own rate: point to a quote instead.

rules.title: A survey rate needs its source and a not-an-offer line
rules.append: Rates shown are Freddie Mac PMMS weekly national averages, not a quote or an offer of credit. Your own rate depends on your situation.
rules.message: A rate quoted from Freddie Mac's survey is an average, not what you offer. Name the source and say it is not an offer. Not applied to a post that states your own APR: then the offer rules apply instead.
rules.source: Reg N (MAP Rule), 12 CFR 1014.3(b); Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.24(c)

rules.title: Loan officer and company NMLS ID
rules.message: State rules require the originator's name and NMLS ID (and usually the company's) on advertising, including social media. Maryland accepts the ID on the profile instead; this bundle adds it to every post. Both numbers are required: the check passes only when two NMLS IDs are present.
rules.source: SAFE Act state rules; Texas SML RMLO social media requirements (2025); COMAR 09.03.06.06

rules.title: Equal Housing Opportunity or Lender statement
rules.message: Mortgage ads carry the Equal Housing statement your company uses: the profile's eho_statement (a lender that prints 'Equal Housing Lender' puts that there), or 'Equal Housing Opportunity' when it is empty. It is a legal requirement for some lenders (FDIC-supervised banks: 'Equal Housing Lender') and a policy of most others; this bundle adds it to every post by default. To switch it off, set equal_housing_line: off in profile.md, only on your compliance team's written say-so.
rules.source: 12 CFR 338.3 (FDIC-supervised lenders); 12 CFR 701.31 (federal credit unions); HUD Equal Housing Opportunity logo guidance; lender and investor policy (not verified as a federal rule for every originator)

rules.title: Guaranteed approval or 'everyone qualifies'
rules.message: Approval depends on underwriting. Promising it misrepresents the terms of credit. Say what you will do instead (review options, explain programs).
rules.source: Reg N (MAP Rule), 12 CFR 1014.3; FTC Act §5

rules.title: Possible implied government affiliation
rules.message: FHA, VA and USDA loans are government-insured or guaranteed, but you are not the government. Do not suggest an official program, a government grant for all, or an endorsement.
rules.source: Reg N (MAP Rule), 12 CFR 1014.3(n); Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.24(i)(3)

rules.title: Rate forecast stated as a fact
if_any: \brates (will|are going to|are about to)( \w+){0,2} (drop|fall|go down|come down|rise|go up|spike|crash)\b
rules.message: Nobody knows next week's rate. Say what happened (the survey), not what will happen, or attribute a forecast to its source.
rules.source: Reg N (MAP Rule), 12 CFR 1014.3(b); FTC Act §5

rules.title: 'Fixed' next to an adjustable product
if_any: \b(ARM|adjustable)\b[^.\n]{0,40}\bfixed( rate| payment)? (for life|for the life of the loan|forever)\b
rules.message: An adjustable-rate product is fixed only for its initial period. Say how long, and that it adjusts after.
rules.source: Reg N (MAP Rule), 12 CFR 1014.3(g); Regulation Z, 12 CFR 1026.24(i)(1)

rules.title: Realtor co-marketing that may look like a referral payment
if_any: \b(referral fee|paid partner|pay for referrals|kickback|split the cost of (the )?ad)\b
rules.message: Co-marketing is fine when each party pays its share at fair value. Anything that reads as paying or being paid for referrals is a RESPA Section 8 risk; check with your compliance team.
rules.source: RESPA §8, 12 U.S.C. 2607; Regulation X, 12 CFR 1024.14; CFPB Compliance Bulletin 2015-05

rules.title: Wording that may target or exclude a protected class
rules.message: Fair lending and fair housing rules bar ads that indicate a preference based on familial status, age-linked proxies, religion, national origin, race, sex or disability. Describe the loan, not the borrower.
rules.source: Equal Credit Opportunity Act / Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.4(b); Fair Housing Act 42 U.S.C. 3604(c)

rules.title: Superlative no one can verify
rules.message: 'Lowest rates in town' needs proof the post shows. Use a specific, sourced fact from facts.md instead.
rules.source: FTC Act §5; Reg N (MAP Rule), 12 CFR 1014.3

rules.title: Calling yourself a counselor
rules.message: Reg Z bars mortgage advertisers from calling themselves 'counselor' unless they are a nonprofit counseling service or HUD-certified housing counselor. Use 'loan officer' or 'mortgage advisor' only as your company allows.

rules.title: Points or a finance charge amount is a trigger term
rules.message: The amount of any finance charge (points, a dollar figure for fees) is a trigger term: the down payment, terms and APR must follow. Usual fix: talk about points without a number.
